ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure has 1 center circle, with 10 outer circles evenly arranged around it; every diameter passes through the center circle and connects a pair of opposite outer circles, so there are 5 diameters in total, and each diameter has 3 circles on it. Then reason: Let the center number be c. The sum on each diameter is c+a+b, and these 5 sums are required to all be odd. Therefore: if c is even, then each pair of opposite outer circles must be one odd and one even; if c is odd, then each pair of opposite outer circles must have the same parity. The problem says one of the sums is the smallest possible. The smallest sum of 3 different numbers chosen from 0 to 10 is 0+1+2=3, so this smallest sum must be 3, and that diameter is exactly 0, 1, 2. Therefore the center can only be one of 0, 1, 2: - When c=0, the outer circles paired must be one odd and one even, and the largest other diameter is at most 0+10+9=19. - When c=1, the outer circles paired must have the same parity, 10 and 9 cannot be on the same diameter, and the largest other diameter is at most 1+10+8=19. - When c=2, the outer circles paired must be one odd and one even, 9 and 10 can be paired together, so another diameter can reach 2+9+10=21; the remaining numbers can also continue to be paired as pairs of opposite parity. So the maximum possible remaining sum is 21.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as 10 outer circles arranged around one central circle, with 5 diameters; each diameter consists of two opposite outer circles plus the central circle. From the text, assign the numbers 0 through 10 bijectively to the 11 circles and require all 5 diameter sums to be odd. Let the central number be c. The smallest possible sum of any three distinct numbers from 0 to 10 is 0+1+2=3, and it is odd, so the given smallest possible diameter sum must be 3 and must use exactly the numbers 0, 1, and 2. Then split into the three possible choices for the center in that diameter: c=0 with opposite pair 1,2; c=1 with pair 0,2; c=2 with pair 0,1. Use the parity condition: if c is even, every opposite outer pair must have odd sum, so each pair is one even and one odd; if c is odd, every opposite pair must have even sum, so each pair is same parity. In each case, maximize another diameter sum using the remaining numbers. The c=0 case gives at most 0+10+9=19; the c=1 case cannot use 9 and 10 together because same-parity pairs are required, so gives at most 1+10+8=19; the c=2 case allows pairing 9 and 10, giving 2+9+10=21, and the leftover numbers can still be paired one even with one odd. Therefore the largest possible remaining sum is 21.

Therefore: if c is even, then each pair of opposite outer circles must be one odd and one even; if c is odd, then each pair of opposite outer circles must have the same parity. The problem says one of the sums is the smallest possible. The smallest sum of 3 different numbers chosen from 0 to 10 is 0+1+2=3, so this smallest sum must be 3, and that diameter is exactly 0, 1, 2.
Therefore the center can only be one of 0, 1, 2:

- When c=1, the outer circles paired must have the same parity, 10 and 9 cannot be on the same diameter, and the largest other diameter is at most 1+10+8=19.
- When c=2, the outer circles paired must be one odd and one even, 9 and 10 can be paired together, so another diameter can reach 2+9+10=21; the remaining numbers can also continue to be paired as pairs of opposite parity.
So the maximum possible remaining sum is 21.
